title: How to count only visible rows after filtering
task: A count that respects the filter — "showing N of M records".

excel.note: 103 = COUNTA over visible rows only. Put it ABOVE the data or beside it, not in a filterable row.

explanation: Plain COUNTA keeps counting rows a filter has hidden; SUBTOTAL with the 100-series COUNTA code (103) counts only what's visible (all 3 here since nothing's filtered — apply a filter and the number drops live). A "showing X of Y" header is =SUBTOTAL(103,A2:A1000)&" of "&COUNTA(A2:A1000). Codes 109/101 do the same for SUM/AVERAGE, and the full code table lives in the SUM-vs-SUBTOTAL comparison. Place the formula outside the filtered range or it can hide itself.
